title: Prevent cross-tenant DNS cache stitching caused by SNAT port coalescing
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent resolution of other tenants' hostnames after large scale-down events or peering failovers. Impact pattern: within 30s-2m after scale-down or peering swap, some tenant requests to private hostnames went to a different tenant's service. Investigation targeted DNS caches, conntrack state, and host SNAT behavior on dedicated pool nodes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision two tenants on the same dedicated GPU host pool with egress enabled via shared host SNAT (masquerade).
2) Establish long-lived outbound TLS connections from both tenants to external resolvers and to private in-cluster service IPs, creating conntrack and SNAT mappings.
3) Trigger scale-down of one tenant's replica set and immediately trigger a VPC peering reroute (simulate peering swap).
4) Observe DNS resolution for the scaled-down tenant: sometimes responses returned IPs that belonged to the other tenant and subsequent connections were accepted until TTL/conns expired.
root_cause: A confluence of factors: host-level SNAT port reuse combined with conntrack coalescing and our cached external-resolver fallback logic. When endpoints moved during scale-down/peering swap, conntrack entries and ephemeral SNAT ports were reused and responses from the external resolver were associated with the wrong tenant namespace. Our eBPF-based egress tagging did not cover a small code path used during resolver fallback, so responses arriving via the host stack lacked tenant context and were stitched into another tenant's cache.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Emergency rollback of resolver-fallback-to-external for affected dedicated pools (disabled on 2026-02-19; reverted client to in-namespace resolvers).
2) Forced conntrack flush on impacted nodes using curated drain script (nodes drained and restarted over 2026-02-19 to 2026-02-20).
3) Temporarily increase SNAT port allocation per-tenant on top-of-rack NAT (reduces immediate reuse probability).
4) Customer communications: sent targeted incident notices to three affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix.
long_term_fix: A) Expand eBPF egress tagging to cover resolver fallback and non-proxy reply paths so packet context cannot be lost when responses re-enter the host network stack.
B) Implement per-tenant SNAT port pinning (soft reservation) to minimize port reuse collisions during churn.
C) Add conservative conntrack aging for DNS response flows originating from external resolvers when tenant topology changes are detected (scale events/peering changes).
D) Add end-to-end test that simulates scale-down + peering swap and validates no cross-tenant DNS resolution occurs, to be run in CI and as part of upgrade canaries.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: validation in staging - deploy eBPF fix and SNAT port pinning to a staging dedicated pool and run stress scenario (target: 48h, 2026-02-24 to 2026-02-25).
Phase 1: canary - enable on 2% of dedicated capacity with synthetic traffic and 1 pilot customer (monitoring for 72h, 2026-02-26 to 2026-02-28).
Phase 2: ramp to 25% with automated rollbacks on anomaly triggers (48-72h), coordinate with SRE for escalation playbook.
Phase 3: full rollout to remaining dedicated pools after 96h stable canary window plus sign-off from security and SRE.
qa_steps: - Run CI synthetic: concurrent tenant churn + DNS stress test (no cross-tenant resolves allowed).
- Inject peering failover events and confirm conntrack entries do not cause stale bindbacks.
- Verify eBPF metrics: every outbound packet in fallback path shows tenant tag; responses without tag are dropped/flagged in staging.
- End-to-end: confirm no leakage on TLS session resumption across tenant boundaries after scale events.
notes_updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket created after first customer escalations received overnight. Initial triage assigned to networking on-call.
2026-02-19: Emergency mitigation executed: disabled external resolver fallback on affected pools; conntrack flush initiated. Initial customer impact reduced.
2026-02-20: Identified eBPF tag gap in fallback code path. Prototype patch prepared and bench-tested locally against repro harness.
2026-02-22: SNAT port soft-reservation design approved by infra lead (A. Kumar). Security review flagged potential K8s privilege change; mitigations noted.
2026-02-24: Staging rollout started for eBPF + SNAT changes. Staging passed initial 24h run without leakage.
2026-03-02: Canary metrics look good. No new cross-tenant DNS resolves observed. Preparing release notes and runbook updates.
